forces.title: Upcoming tax rule changes to impact Norwegian new car sales
forces.description: New tax rules anticipated towards the end of 2026 are expected to stimulate a pick-up in new car sales in Norway. This policy change acts as a positive cyclical force, encouraging consumers to make purchases in anticipation of or response to the new regulations. However, the overall sales volume for 2026 is still forecasted to be lower than 2025, reflecting broader economic or market conditions that temper the positive impact of the tax changes. The impact is considered medium as it creates a short-term boost but doesn't fully offset a weaker year.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Electrified vehicles gaining dominant market share in Ireland
forces.description: The market share of electrified vehicles (Hybrid, EV, Plug-In Hybrid) has substantially increased, exceeding 56% in Ireland by 2025, with Electric Vehicles achieving a record 35% growth over 2024. This trend signifies a profound consumer shift towards lower-emission powertrains. For Passenger Vehicle manufacturers, this constitutes a powerful tailwind, necessitating accelerated investment in EV and hybrid research, development, and production capacities to meet evolving consumer demand and capitalize on this rapidly expanding segment of the market.

forces.title: Petrol and diesel powertrain market share declines in Ireland
forces.description: The Irish automotive market is experiencing a continuous and notable decline in the market share held by traditional petrol and diesel vehicles. This represents a fundamental structural change in the industry, driven by environmental concerns, regulatory shifts, and evolving consumer preferences towards more sustainable transport solutions. Passenger Vehicle manufacturers must strategically adapt their product portfolios and long-term production plans to align with this irreversible trend, ensuring competitiveness and compliance in a rapidly decarbonizing market.

forces.title: Lower interest rates and retailer incentives boost Irish car demand
forces.description: The Irish new car market is currently experiencing a period of buoyant demand, significantly supported by a favorable combination of lower interest rates and highly competitive incentives provided by retailers for both new and used vehicles. These factors directly enhance consumer affordability and purchasing power, acting as a crucial tailwind for the Passenger Vehicle sector. This stimulus helps drive increased sales volumes, counteracting the potential dampening effects of ongoing inflationary pressures and broader cost-of-living challenges.

forces.title: EV adoption's reliance on incentives creates market vulnerability
forces.description: The positive trajectory of new car registrations, particularly for Electric Vehicles (EVs) in Ireland, is substantially propped up by various incentives and grants. This dependency presents a critical key risk, as any future reduction or discontinuation of these supportive fiscal measures could significantly dampen consumer demand for EVs. Furthermore, the inherent higher upfront cost for consumers transitioning to electric vehicles and the potential for pressure on used-car values add layers of market vulnerability, demanding careful strategic planning from manufacturers.

viewpoints.title: Norwegian new car sales expected to rebound late 2026 due to tax changes
viewpoints.description: Norwegian car dealers anticipate a significant recovery in new car sales towards the end of 2026, primarily driven by the impending implementation of new tax rules. However, despite this expected positive momentum and policy-driven stimulus, the broader market outlook suggests that total sales volumes for 2026 are still projected to be weaker compared to the previous year, 2025. This indicates a nuanced, cautiously optimistic near-term perspective, where specific policy changes offer a clear tailwind but are tempered by other, possibly macroeconomic, factors impacting overall demand.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Irish new car registrations buoyant, driven by electrification and incentives
viewpoints.description: Ireland's new car registrations are exhibiting a robust and positive trend, marked by a 3% increase in 2025 compared to 2024. This market buoyancy is primarily underpinned by a combination of lower interest rates and highly competitive incentives offered by retailers. Crucially, electrified vehicles (Hybrid, EV, Plug-In Hybrid) now command over 56% of the market, with full electric vehicles alone seeing a record 35% growth. This reflects a strong consumer shift towards electrification despite broader inflationary pressures.

demand_drivers.description: Reduced borrowing costs make car purchases more affordable for consumers, stimulating demand for new vehicles.
Competitive offers and promotional deals from retailers for both new and used cars attract buyers and drive sales volumes.
Increasing adoption of electrified vehicles (Hybrid, EV, Plug-In Hybrid) fuels market growth, particularly EVs which saw record growth.

market_sizing.methodology: Total new car registrations for the full year 2025 in Ireland, reflecting actual sales volumes.
